card.title_ko: 외상에서의 트라넥삼산(TXA): NAEMSP·ACEP·ACS-COT 합동 입장문 및 자료 문서
card.scope_ko: 병원 전(EMS·구급) 단계에서 외상 환자에게 정맥/골내(IV/IO)로 투여하는 트라넥삼산(TXA)의 사용을 다룬다. 주로 출혈성 쇼크 임상 징후를 보이는 성인 외상 환자가 대상이며, 소아 외상 환자에 대한 별도 언급을 포함한다. 2016년 지침을 새 근거로 갱신한 문서다.
summary: Prehospital TXA may reduce mortality in adult trauma patients with hemorrhagic shock when administered AFTER lifesaving interventions; it should not be prioritized above more evidence-based lifesaving measures (based on moderate- to high-quality but mixed, indirect evidence).
Prehospital TXA appears safe, with low risk of thromboembolic events or seizure (meta-analysis found no significant association with VTE or seizures).

Optimal dose/rate/route is undetermined; EMS agencies may give either a 1-g IV/IO dose followed by a hospital-based 1-g infusion over 8 hours (CRASH-2 regimen), OR a 2-g IV/IO dose as an infusion or slow push.

If used, give only to adults with clinical signs of hemorrhagic shock and no later than 3 hours post-injury, with preference for administration within 1 hour; no benefit shown beyond 3 hours or in patients without clinically significant bleeding.
Pediatric prehospital TXA for hemorrhagic shock has not been studied and standardized dosing is not established; if used, it should be given within 3 hours of injury.
Prehospital TXA administration must be clearly communicated to receiving clinicians to ensure appropriate monitoring and avoid duplicate dosing.

A multidisciplinary team led by EMS physicians (with EMS clinicians, emergency physicians, and trauma surgeons) should run a quality-improvement program assessing protocol compliance and clinical complications.
summary_ko: 병원 전 TXA는 출혈성 쇼크가 있는 성인 외상 환자에서 생명구조 처치(lifesaving interventions) 이후에 투여할 때 사망률을 줄일 수 있다. 단, 근거가 더 확실한 생명구조 조치보다 우선순위를 두어서는 안 된다(중등도~높은 질이나 결과가 혼재된 간접 근거 기반).
병원 전 TXA는 안전해 보이며, 혈전색전증이나 경련 위험이 낮다(메타분석에서 VTE·경련과 유의한 연관 없음).
최적 용량·속도·경로는 미확정이다. EMS 기관은 ①1 g IV/IO 후 병원에서 1 g을 8시간에 걸쳐 주입(CRASH-2 방식) 또는 ②2 g IV/IO를 주입 또는 느린 푸시로 투여하는 두 방식 중 하나를 쓸 수 있다.
사용한다면 출혈성 쇼크의 임상 징후가 있는 성인에게, 손상 후 늦어도 3시간 이내(가급적 1시간 이내)에 투여한다. 3시간을 넘기거나 임상적으로 유의한 출혈이 없는 환자에서는 이득이 입증되지 않았다.
소아 병원 전 TXA는 출혈성 쇼크에 대해 연구된 바가 없고 표준 용량도 정립되지 않았다. 사용한다면 손상 후 3시간 이내에 투여한다.
병원 전 TXA 투여는 인계받는 의료진에게 명확히 전달하여 적절한 모니터링과 중복 투여 방지를 도모해야 한다.
EMS 의사가 주도하고 EMS 임상가·응급의학과 의사·외상외과 의사가 참여하는 다학제 팀이 프로토콜 준수와 임상 합병증을 평가하는 질 향상(QI) 프로그램을 운영해야 한다.

keyChanges.topic: 용량 옵션 확대(1 g+주입 → 2 g 단회 옵션 추가)
keyChanges.detail: The 2016-era standard was the CRASH-2 regimen: 1-g IV bolus over 10 min followed by a 1-g infusion over 8 h. The 2025 update, incorporating newer prehospital and combat-casualty evidence, now additionally accepts a single 2-g IV/IO dose given as an infusion or slow push as an acceptable alternative, reflecting interest in a faster, simpler prehospital regimen (e.g., the single 2-g IV push recommended for combat casualties by the Joint Trauma System DCR guideline). The optimal regimen remains formally undetermined.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 2016년 당시 표준은 CRASH-2 방식(1 g을 10분에 걸쳐 정주 후 8시간에 걸쳐 1 g 추가 주입)이었다. 2025년 갱신본은 새로운 병원 전·전투 사상자 근거를 반영하여, 2 g 단회 용량을 주입 또는 느린 푸시로 투여하는 방식을 추가 허용 옵션으로 인정한다. 이는 더 빠르고 단순한 병원 전 투여에 대한 요구(예: Joint Trauma System DCR 지침의 전투 사상자용 2 g 단회 IV 푸시)를 반영한 것이다. 다만 최적 용법은 여전히 공식적으로 미확정이다.

keyChanges.detail: The update emphasizes TXA as an adjunct given AFTER lifesaving interventions and explicitly states it should not be prioritized above more evidence-based lifesaving measures. It reaffirms a ≤3-hour window but adds a stated preference for <1 hour (a post hoc analysis showed a 7.9% 30-day mortality reduction only when given within 1 h of injury, not 1–3 h), and adds that no benefit is seen beyond 3 h or in patients without clinically significant bleeding.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 갱신본은 TXA를 생명구조 처치(lifesaving interventions) 이후에 주는 보조 요법으로 강조하고, 근거가 더 확실한 생명구조 조치보다 우선해서는 안 된다고 명시한다. 3시간 이내 원칙을 재확인하되 1시간 이내 투여를 선호한다고 추가했다(사후 분석에서 손상 후 1시간 이내 투여에서만 30일 사망률 7.9% 감소, 1~3시간에서는 없음). 또한 3시간을 넘기거나 임상적으로 유의한 출혈이 없는 환자에서는 이득이 없다고 덧붙였다.

keyChanges.detail: The update explicitly addresses pediatric trauma, stating that prehospital TXA for pediatric patients with hemorrhagic shock has not been studied and no standardized dosing has been established, and that if used it should be given within 3 hours of injury — an explicit acknowledgment of the pediatric evidence gap.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 갱신본은 소아 외상을 명시적으로 다뤄, 출혈성 쇼크가 있는 소아에 대한 병원 전 TXA는 연구된 바 없고 표준 용량도 정립되지 않았으며, 사용한다면 손상 후 3시간 이내에 투여해야 한다고 밝혔다 — 소아 근거 공백을 명시적으로 인정한 것이다.

keyChanges.topic: 인계 시 소통 및 질 향상(QI) 체계
keyChanges.detail: The update adds explicit systems recommendations not emphasized in 2016: prehospital TXA administration must be clearly communicated to receiving clinicians to avoid duplicate dosing and ensure monitoring, and an EMS-physician-led multidisciplinary team should operate a QI program to audit protocol compliance and identify complications.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 갱신본은 2016년에 강조되지 않던 시스템 차원의 권고를 추가했다: 병원 전 TXA 투여는 중복 투여 방지와 모니터링을 위해 인계 의료진에게 명확히 전달해야 하며, EMS 의사가 주도하는 다학제 팀이 프로토콜 준수 감사와 합병증 파악을 위한 QI 프로그램을 운영해야 한다.

card.practiceImpact: For EMS and EM/CCM teams, TXA remains an adjunct — not a substitute — for hemorrhage control and resuscitation: reserve it for adults with clear hemorrhagic-shock signs, give it after lifesaving interventions, and target within 1 hour (never beyond 3 hours) of injury. Either the classic 1-g bolus + 1-g/8-h infusion or a single 2-g IV/IO dose is acceptable, so agencies can adopt the simpler 2-g regimen prehospitally if desired. Because prehospital dosing is now common, receiving trauma/EM teams must confirm whether and when TXA was already given to avoid re-dosing and to plan the in-hospital infusion. Do not routinely give TXA to patients without significant bleeding, and treat pediatric use as unproven with no standardized dose.
card.practiceImpact_ko: EMS 및 응급·중환자 팀에게 TXA는 출혈 조절·소생술의 보조 수단이지 대체물이 아니다. 출혈성 쇼크 징후가 뚜렷한 성인에 한정하고, 생명구조 처치 이후에 투여하며, 손상 후 1시간 이내(절대 3시간 초과 금지)를 목표로 한다. 고전적 1 g 볼루스+8시간 1 g 주입 또는 2 g 단회 IV/IO 중 어느 쪽도 허용되므로, 원한다면 병원 전 단계에서 더 단순한 2 g 방식을 채택할 수 있다. 병원 전 투여가 흔해진 만큼, 인계받는 외상·응급 팀은 TXA가 이미 언제 투여됐는지 반드시 확인해 중복 투여를 피하고 병원 내 주입 계획을 세워야 한다. 유의한 출혈이 없는 환자에게 일상적으로 투여하지 말고, 소아 사용은 표준 용량이 없는 미검증 영역으로 취급한다.

published.title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Tranexamic Acid in Trauma - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACEP, and ACS-COT.
published.abstract: Prehospital use of tranexamic acid (TXA) has grown substantially over the past decade despite contradictory evidence supporting its widespread use. Since the previous guidance document on the prehospital use of TXA for injured patients was published by the National Association of Emergency Medical Services Physicians (NAEMSP), the American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), and the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) in 2016, new research has investigated outcomes of patients who receive TXA in the prehospital setting. To provide updated evidence-based guidance on the use of intravenous TXA for injured patients in the EMS setting, we performed a structured literature review and developed the following recommendations supported by the evidence summarized in the accompanying resource document.

card.title_ko: 병원전 외상 개요서(Prehospital Trauma Compendium): 외상에서의 트라넥삼산(TXA) — NAEMSP·ACEP·ACS-COT 공동 입장문 및 자료 문서
card.scope_ko: 병원전(EMS) 환경에서 손상 환자에게 정맥내(IV/IO) 트라넥삼산(TXA)을 투여하는 것에 대한 근거 기반 지침으로, 주로 출혈성 쇼크의 임상 징후가 있는 성인 외상 환자를 대상으로 한다. 2016년 NAEMSP·ACS-COT·ACEP 공동 지침을 갱신한 개정판이며, 소아 외상에서의 TXA 역할과 미해결 지점도 함께 다룬다.
summary: Prehospital TXA administration may reduce mortality in adult trauma patients with hemorrhagic shock when given after lifesaving interventions.

Acceptable dosing options are either a 1 g IV/IO dose followed by a hospital-based 1 g infusion over 8 hours, OR a single 2 g IV/IO dose given as an infusion or slow push; the optimal regimen remains unresolved.

If used, prehospital TXA should be given to adult trauma patients with clinical signs of hemorrhagic shock and no later than 3 hours post-injury; there is no evidence of benefit beyond 3 hours or in patients without clinically significant bleeding.
TXA appears safe in this setting, with low risk of thromboembolic events and seizures.
The role of prehospital TXA in pediatric trauma patients with signs of hemorrhagic shock has not been studied and standardized pediatric dosing has not been established.

A multidisciplinary quality-improvement program led by EMS physicians and including EMS clinicians, emergency physicians, and trauma surgeons should monitor prehospital TXA for protocol compliance and identification of clinical complications.
summary_ko: 병원전 TXA 투여는 생명구조 처치(lifesaving interventions) 이후에 투여할 경우 출혈성 쇼크를 동반한 성인 외상 환자의 사망률을 낮출 수 있다.
허용되는 용량 옵션은 ① 1 g IV/IO 투여 후 병원에서 1 g을 8시간에 걸쳐 주입, 또는 ② 2 g IV/IO 단회 용량을 주입 또는 천천히 정주(slow push)하는 방식이며, 최적 용법은 아직 미확정이다.
사용한다면 출혈성 쇼크의 임상 징후가 있는 성인 외상 환자에게 손상 후 3시간 이내에 투여해야 하며, 3시간을 넘기거나 임상적으로 유의한 출혈이 없는 환자에서는 이득의 근거가 없다.
이 환경에서 TXA는 혈전색전증 및 경련 위험이 낮아 안전한 것으로 보인다.
출혈성 쇼크 징후가 있는 소아 외상 환자에서의 병원전 TXA 역할은 연구되지 않았고 표준 소아 용량도 확립되지 않았다.
EMS 의사가 주도하고 EMS 임상가·응급의학과 의사·외상외과 의사가 포함된 다학제 질 향상(QI) 프로그램이 프로토콜 준수와 임상 합병증 파악을 위해 병원전 TXA 투여를 모니터링해야 한다.

keyChanges.detail: The 2025 update explicitly endorses a single 2 g IV/IO dose (given as an infusion or slow push) as an acceptable alternative to the traditional split regimen of 1 g IV/IO followed by a hospital-based 1 g infusion over 8 hours, and states the optimal regimen remains unresolved. This adds an operationally simpler single-bolus option not emphasized in the 2016 document, reflecting newer prehospital evidence.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 2025년 개정판은 기존의 분할 용법(1 g IV/IO 후 병원에서 1 g을 8시간 주입)에 더해, 단회 2 g IV/IO(주입 또는 slow push) 용법을 허용 가능한 대안으로 명시하고 최적 용법은 미확정이라고 밝힌다. 이는 2016년 문서에서 부각되지 않았던 운영상 더 단순한 단회 볼루스 옵션을 새로 반영한 것으로, 최신 병원전 연구 근거를 반영한 변화다.

keyChanges.detail: The update tightens patient selection to adult trauma patients with clinical signs of hemorrhagic shock and specifies administration after lifesaving interventions and no later than 3 hours post-injury, explicitly stating there is no evidence of benefit beyond 3 hours or in patients without clinically significant bleeding — a more restrictive, shock-directed framing than broad prehospital use.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 개정판은 대상을 출혈성 쇼크의 임상 징후가 있는 성인 외상 환자로 좁히고, 생명구조 처치 이후 그리고 손상 후 3시간 이내 투여를 명시하며, 3시간 이후나 임상적으로 유의한 출혈이 없는 환자에서는 이득의 근거가 없다고 못 박는다 — 광범위한 병원전 사용보다 쇼크 중심으로 더 제한적인 틀이다.

keyChanges.detail: The 2025 statement adds an explicit safety conclusion that prehospital TXA carries a low risk of thromboembolic events and seizures, providing reassurance that was not firmly established at the time of the 2016 guidance.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 2025년 입장문은 병원전 TXA가 혈전색전증 및 경련 위험이 낮다는 안전성 결론을 명시적으로 추가했으며, 이는 2016년 지침 시점에는 확립되지 않았던 안심 근거를 제공한다.

keyChanges.detail: The update explicitly states that the role of prehospital TXA in pediatric trauma patients with signs of hemorrhagic shock has not been studied and that standardized pediatric dosing has not been established, formally flagging this as an evidence gap rather than extrapolating adult practice.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 개정판은 출혈성 쇼크 징후가 있는 소아 외상 환자에서 병원전 TXA의 역할이 연구되지 않았고 표준 소아 용량도 확립되지 않았음을 명시하여, 성인 진료를 외삽하지 않고 이를 근거 공백으로 공식화한다.

keyChanges.detail: The 2025 document adds a governance requirement that a multidisciplinary team led by EMS physicians (including EMS clinicians, emergency physicians, and trauma surgeons) develop a quality-improvement program to audit protocol compliance and identify clinical complications of prehospital TXA.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 2025년 문서는 EMS 의사가 주도하고 EMS 임상가·응급의학과 의사·외상외과 의사가 포함된 다학제 팀이 병원전 TXA의 프로토콜 준수를 감사하고 임상 합병증을 파악하는 질 향상(QI) 프로그램을 구축하도록 하는 거버넌스 요건을 추가했다.

card.practiceImpact: EMS systems and receiving trauma/EM teams should target prehospital TXA to adult patients with clinical signs of hemorrhagic shock, give it after lifesaving interventions and within 3 hours of injury, and stop offering it for undifferentiated trauma or late presentations where benefit is unproven. Systems may standardize on a single 2 g IV/IO dose to simplify field administration, or retain the 1 g + 1 g/8 h regimen, coordinating the second-gram infusion with the receiving hospital. Clinicians can be reassured about a low thromboembolic and seizure risk, but should not extrapolate to children given the absence of pediatric data, and should build an EMS-physician-led QI loop to audit compliance and complications.
card.practiceImpact_ko: EMS 시스템과 수용 외상/응급팀은 병원전 TXA를 출혈성 쇼크의 임상 징후가 있는 성인 환자에 한정해 생명구조 처치 이후·손상 3시간 이내에 투여하고, 이득이 입증되지 않은 미분류 외상이나 지연 도착 환자에서는 사용을 중단해야 한다. 현장 투여 단순화를 위해 단회 2 g IV/IO로 표준화하거나, 1 g + 8시간 1 g 용법을 유지하되 두 번째 1 g 주입은 수용 병원과 협의해 연계할 수 있다. 낮은 혈전색전증·경련 위험으로 안심할 수 있으나 소아 데이터 부재로 아동에게 외삽해서는 안 되며, 준수 여부와 합병증을 감사하는 EMS 의사 주도 QI 체계를 구축해야 한다.

published.title: A Critical Review of the 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.
published.abstract: The Utstein Formula for Survival, the ethos of the American Heart Association's 2025 guidelines for cardiopulmonary resuscitation and emergency cardiovascular care, is a conceptual model for survival of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest that equally weighs medical science, educational efficiency, and local implementation. With this formula in mind, the American Heart Association has put forth new guidelines that emphasize not only high-quality chest compressions and early defibrillation but also robust systems of care, equitable access, advanced resuscitation techniques, and postcardiac arrest recovery. The 2025 updates carry significant weight for health policy, clinical practice, education, and ethical discussions. In this review, we highlight the major changes, discuss their implications, and propose directions for future research and implementation.

card.title_ko: 2025 미국심장협회(AHA) 심폐소생술 및 응급심혈관치료(CPR·ECC) 가이드라인에 대한 비판적 고찰
card.scope_ko: 심정지(원내·원외, 신생아·소아·성인 전 연령) 환자에 대한 기본소생술(BLS)·전문소생술(ALS)·심정지 후 관리·특수상황·시스템·교육·윤리를 포괄하는 AHA 2025 CPR/ECC 종합 가이드라인을 다룬다. 본 논문 자체는 이 가이드라인의 주요 변화와 함의를 정리·비판적으로 검토한 리뷰이다.
summary: Anchor the whole guideline on the Utstein Formula for Survival — survival depends equally on medical science, educational efficiency, and local implementation — not on science alone.
Reaffirm the fundamentals: high-quality chest compressions (adequate rate/depth, full recoil, minimal interruptions) and early defibrillation as the highest-yield interventions.
Build robust, coordinated systems of care with attention to equitable access, and add a unified single Chain of Survival spanning all ages and settings with a Recovery/survivorship link.
Incorporate advanced resuscitation techniques and structured post–cardiac arrest care (including temperature management and hemodynamic stabilization) to improve neurological outcomes.
Address ethics and health-policy dimensions explicitly, including a dedicated ethics chapter spanning neonatal to geriatric populations.
The review flags implications for policy, clinical practice, education, and ethics, and proposes directions for future research and implementation.
summary_ko: 가이드라인 전체를 Utstein Formula for Survival에 정박한다 — 생존은 의학적 과학뿐 아니라 교육 효율성과 지역 실행이 동등한 비중으로 결정된다.
기본을 재확인한다: 고품질 흉부압박(적정 속도·깊이, 완전 이완, 중단 최소화)과 조기 제세동이 가장 효과가 큰 개입이다.
형평적 접근을 고려한 견고하고 조율된 치료 시스템을 구축하고, 전 연령·전 장소에 적용되며 회복/생존자 관리 고리를 포함하는 단일 통합 Chain of Survival을 도입한다.
진보된 소생 기법과 체계적인 심정지 후 관리(체온 관리, 혈역학 안정화 포함)를 통합해 신경학적 예후를 개선한다.
신생아부터 노년까지 아우르는 별도의 윤리 챕터를 포함하여 윤리·보건정책 차원을 명시적으로 다룬다.
본 리뷰는 정책·임상·교육·윤리적 함의를 짚고 향후 연구·실행 방향을 제안한다.

keyChanges.detail: For adults in cardiac arrest, initial attempts at IV access are now recommended over initial attempts at IO access, with IO reserved for when initial IV attempts are unsuccessful — a shift emphasizing IV as the preferred first route rather than treating IV and IO as interchangeable.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 성인 심정지에서 이제 최초 접근은 IO보다 IV를 우선 시도하도록 권고하며, 최초 IV 시도가 실패한 경우에만 IO를 시도한다. IV와 IO를 동등하게 취급하던 것에서 IV를 우선 경로로 명확히 한 변화다.

keyChanges.detail: Routine use of mechanical CPR devices is no longer recommended for adult cardiac arrest, because multiple RCTs found no survival difference versus manual CPR; mechanical CPR may still be considered in select situations where high-quality manual compressions are impractical or unsafe (e.g., transport, hazardous environments) provided interruptions stay minimal.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 성인 심정지에서 기계식 CPR 장치의 일상적(routine) 사용은 더 이상 권고되지 않는다. 다수의 RCT에서 수기 CPR 대비 생존 차이가 없었기 때문이다. 다만 고품질 수기 압박이 어렵거나 안전하지 않은 특정 상황(이송 중, 위험 환경 등)에서는 중단을 최소화하는 조건으로 여전히 고려할 수 있다.

keyChanges.detail: For choking in conscious adults/children, the sequence now begins with 5 back blows and alternates 5 back blows with 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is cleared or the patient becomes unresponsive — back blows are newly incorporated rather than abdominal thrusts alone.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 의식이 있는 성인·소아의 질식 대응은 이제 5회 등 두드리기(back blows)로 시작해, 이물이 제거되거나 환자가 무반응이 될 때까지 등 두드리기 5회와 복부 밀어내기(abdominal thrusts) 5회를 번갈아 시행한다. 복부 밀어내기만 하던 방식에서 등 두드리기가 새로 편입됐다.

keyChanges.detail: For choking infants, use 5 back blows followed by 5 chest thrusts (heel of one hand); abdominal thrusts are explicitly not recommended in infants because of injury risk.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 질식 영아에게는 5회 등 두드리기 후 (한 손 손꿈치로) 5회 흉부 압박(chest thrusts)을 시행한다. 영아에게 복부 밀어내기는 손상 위험 때문에 명시적으로 권고하지 않는다.

keyChanges.detail: Delayed umbilical cord clamping for newborns is extended from at least 30 seconds to at least 60 seconds, to improve neonatal blood volume/iron stores.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 신생아 제대 결찰(cord clamping) 지연 시간이 '최소 30초'에서 '최소 60초'로 연장됐다. 신생아 혈액량·철분 저장을 개선하기 위함이다.

keyChanges.detail: A new opioid overdose response algorithm is added, expanding emphasis on rapid naloxone administration and public access to naloxone (and defibrillation), with recognition of overdose signs (slow breathing, pinpoint pupils, altered consciousness, cyanosis).
keyChanges.detail_ko: 오피오이드 과량 대응 알고리즘이 새로 추가됐다. 신속한 날록손 투여와 날록손(및 제세동)에 대한 공공 접근성 강조가 확대됐고, 과량 징후(느린 호흡, 축소된 동공, 의식 변화, 청색증) 인지가 포함됐다.

keyChanges.detail: The previously separate Chains of Survival (adult/pediatric, in-hospital/out-of-hospital) are consolidated into a single unified Chain applying across all ages and settings, and it now includes a Recovery/survivorship link.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 기존에 나뉘어 있던 Chain of Survival(성인/소아, 원내/원외)이 전 연령·전 장소에 적용되는 단일 통합 Chain으로 합쳐졌으며, 이제 회복/생존자 관리(Recovery/survivorship) 고리가 포함된다.

keyChanges.detail: Terminology is refined — 'rescue breaths' becomes 'breaths' and 'bystander' becomes 'lay rescuer' — to standardize language across the documents.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 용어가 정비됐다 — 'rescue breaths'는 'breaths'로, 'bystander'는 'lay rescuer'로 변경되어 문서 전반의 표현이 표준화됐다.

keyChanges.detail: Defibrillator pad placement guidance is clarified — either anterolateral or anteroposterior positioning is acceptable — and pads greater than 8 cm in diameter are recommended.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 제세동 패드 위치 지침이 명확해졌다 — 전측방(anterolateral) 또는 전후방(anteroposterior) 배치 모두 허용된다 — 그리고 직경 8 cm 초과 패드가 권고된다.

keyChanges.detail: For infants and children in cardiac arrest, pauses in chest compressions should be minimized and kept to less than 10 seconds.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 심정지 영아·소아에서 흉부압박 중단은 최소화하고 10초 미만으로 유지해야 한다.

keyChanges.detail: Renewed emphasis that CPR should be performed on a firm surface whenever possible, with attention to rescuer hand/body position and patient positioning.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 가능하면 CPR을 단단한 표면에서 시행하도록 다시 강조하며, 구조자 손·몸 자세와 환자 체위에 주의하도록 한다.

keyChanges.detail: A new chapter dedicated to the Ethics of CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care is added, covering foundational ethics principles and contemporary challenges from neonatal to geriatric age groups.
keyChanges.detail_ko: CPR 및 응급심혈관치료 윤리를 다루는 새 챕터가 신설됐다. 기초 윤리 원칙과 신생아부터 노년까지의 현대적 윤리 쟁점을 포괄한다.

card.practiceImpact: At the bedside, default to IV access first in adult cardiac arrest and reserve IO for failed IV attempts; stop deploying mechanical CPR devices routinely and rely on high-quality manual compressions, using devices only when manual CPR is impractical. Update BLS/first-aid teaching and airway-obstruction protocols to add back blows (adults/children) and back blows + chest thrusts for infants, and integrate a standing naloxone/opioid-overdose pathway with public-access kits. In the delivery room, extend delayed cord clamping to at least 60 seconds, and adopt the single unified Chain of Survival — including formal recovery/survivorship follow-up — into departmental and EMS protocols.
card.practiceImpact_ko: 현장에서는 성인 심정지 시 IV 접근을 먼저 시도하고 IO는 IV 실패 시로 미룬다. 기계식 CPR 장치의 일상적 사용을 중단하고 고품질 수기 압박에 의존하되, 수기 CPR이 곤란한 경우에만 장치를 쓴다. BLS·응급처치 교육과 기도폐쇄 프로토콜을 갱신해 성인·소아에는 등 두드리기를, 영아에는 등 두드리기+흉부 압박을 반영하고, 공공 접근 키트를 포함한 상시 날록손/오피오이드 과량 대응 경로를 통합한다. 분만실에서는 제대 결찰 지연을 최소 60초로 연장하고, 회복/생존자 추적을 포함한 단일 통합 Chain of Survival을 부서·EMS 프로토콜에 도입한다.

published.title: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) 2025 clinical practice guideline on fluid therapy in adult critically ill patients: part 2-the volume of resuscitation fluids.
published.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on the volume of early resuscitation fluid for adult critically ill patients.
METHODS: An international panel of experts developed the guideline, focusing on fluid resuscitation volume in adult critically ill patients with circulatory failure. Using the PICO format, questions were formulated, and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach was applied to assess evidence and formulate recommendations.
RESULTS: In adults with sepsis or septic shock, the guideline suggests administering up to 30 ml/kg of intravenous crystalloids in the initial phase, with adjustments based on clinical context and frequent reassessments (very low certainty of evidence). We suggest using an individualized approach in the optimization phase (very low certainty of evidence). No recommendation could be made for or against restrictive or liberal fluid strategies in the optimization phase (moderate certainty of no effect). For hemorrhagic shock, a restrictive fluid strategy is suggested after blunt trauma (moderate certainty) and penetrating trauma (low certainty), with fluid administration for non-traumatic hemorrhagic shock guided by hemodynamic and biochemical parameters (ungraded best practice). For circulatory failure due to left-sided cardiogenic shock, fluid resuscitation as the primary treatment is not recommended. Fluids should be administered cautiously for cardiac tamponade until definitive treatment and guided by surrogate markers of right heart congestion in acute pulmonary embolism (ungraded best practice). No recommendation could be made for circulatory failure associated with acute respiratory distress syndrome.
CONCLUSIONS: The panel made four conditional recommendations and four ungraded best practice statements. No recommendations were made for two questions. Knowledge gaps were identified, and suggestions for future research were provided.

card.title_ko: 성인 중환자의 수액 요법에 관한 유럽중환자의학회(ESICM) 2025 임상진료지침: 파트 2 — 소생 수액의 용량
card.scope_ko: 순환부전(쇼크)을 동반한 성인 중환자에서 '초기 소생 수액의 용량'을 다루는 근거기반 지침이다. 패혈증/패혈성 쇼크, 출혈성 쇼크(둔상·관통상·비외상성), 좌심성 심장성 쇼크, 심장압전·급성 폐색전증 등 폐쇄성 쇼크, ARDS 동반 순환부전을 대상으로 하며, 수액의 '종류'(파트 1)와 '제거/탈소생'(파트 3)은 별도 편에서 다룬다.
summary: Sepsis/septic shock, initial (salvage) phase: suggest administering UP TO 30 ml/kg of IV crystalloids, adjusted to clinical context (sepsis source, cardiovascular comorbidity, fluid losses) with frequent reassessment (conditional recommendation, very low certainty).

Sepsis/septic shock, optimization phase: suggest an INDIVIDUALIZED approach (e.g., fluid challenges guided by preload/fluid responsiveness) over a non-individualized strategy (conditional recommendation, very low certainty).
Sepsis/septic shock, optimization phase: NO recommendation for or against a systematically restrictive vs liberal fluid strategy (moderate certainty of no effect, from ~13 trials / 4000+ patients).
Traumatic hemorrhagic shock — penetrating trauma: suggest a RESTRICTIVE fluid strategy with permissive hypotension until hemorrhage control (conditional recommendation, low certainty).

Traumatic hemorrhagic shock — blunt trauma: suggest a RESTRICTIVE fluid strategy (conditional recommendation, moderate certainty); does not apply to intraoperative or post-hemorrhage-control management.
Non-traumatic hemorrhagic shock: guide fluid administration by hemodynamic and biochemical parameters (ungraded best practice statement).
Left-sided cardiogenic shock: fluid resuscitation should NOT be the primary treatment (ungraded best practice statement).

Obstructive shock: give fluids CAUTIOUSLY in cardiac tamponade only as a temporizing measure until definitive drainage, and guide fluids by surrogate markers of right-heart congestion in acute pulmonary embolism (ungraded best practice statements). NO recommendation for circulatory failure associated with ARDS.
summary_ko: 패혈증/패혈성 쇼크, 초기(salvage) 단계: 정맥 결정질액을 최대 30 ml/kg까지 투여하되 임상 맥락(패혈증 원인, 심혈관 동반질환, 수액 손실)에 맞춰 조정하고 자주 재평가할 것을 제안(조건부 권고, 매우 낮은 확실성).
패혈증/패혈성 쇼크, 최적화(optimization) 단계: 비개별화 전략보다 개별화 접근(예: 전부하/수액반응성에 기반한 fluid challenge)을 제안(조건부 권고, 매우 낮은 확실성).
패혈증/패혈성 쇼크, 최적화 단계: 체계적 제한 대 자유 수액 전략에 대해서는 찬반 권고를 하지 않음(효과 없음에 대한 중등도 확실성, 약 13개 시험·4000명 이상).
외상성 출혈성 쇼크 — 관통상: 출혈 조절 전까지 permissive hypotension을 동반한 제한적 수액 전략을 제안(조건부 권고, 낮은 확실성).
외상성 출혈성 쇼크 — 둔상: 제한적 수액 전략을 제안(조건부 권고, 중등도 확실성); 수술 중 또는 출혈 조절 이후 관리에는 적용되지 않음.
비외상성 출혈성 쇼크: 혈역학·생화학 지표에 따라 수액 투여를 조절(등급 미부여 모범진료 성명).
좌심성 심장성 쇼크: 수액 소생을 일차 치료로 삼지 말 것(등급 미부여 모범진료 성명).
폐쇄성 쇼크: 심장압전에서는 확정적 배액 전까지 임시 조치로만 신중히 수액을 투여하고, 급성 폐색전증에서는 우심 울혈의 대리 지표에 따라 수액을 조절(등급 미부여 모범진료 성명). ARDS 동반 순환부전에 대해서는 권고하지 않음.

keyChanges.topic: 패혈증 초기 수액량 (30 ml/kg의 방향 전환)
keyChanges.detail: Versus the Surviving Sepsis Campaign, which recommends at least 30 ml/kg of crystalloid within the first 3 hours (a de-facto minimum floor), ESICM 2025 reframes 30 ml/kg as an UP-TO / maximum reference dose in the initial phase, to be individualized to clinical context and reassessed frequently. Both are weak/conditional recommendations, but ESICM downgrades the certainty to VERY LOW, explicitly noting no RCT directly compares 30 ml/kg to other volumes and that the SSC figure rests on observational data. The reason: rigid weight-based dosing risks harm (e.g., worse outcomes with protocolized large-volume care in resource-limited settings) and ignores patient-specific factors.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 적어도 30 ml/kg를 3시간 내 투여하도록 한 Surviving Sepsis Campaign(사실상 하한선)과 달리, ESICM 2025는 30 ml/kg를 초기 단계의 '상한/최대 기준(up to)'으로 재정의하고 임상 맥락에 맞춰 개별화·빈번한 재평가를 하도록 했다. 두 지침 모두 약한/조건부 권고이지만 ESICM은 확실성을 '매우 낮음'으로 낮췄는데, 30 ml/kg를 다른 용량과 직접 비교한 RCT가 없고 SSC 수치가 관찰연구에 근거한다는 점을 명시했다. 이유: 체중 기반의 경직된 고정 용량은 해를 줄 수 있고(예: 자원 제한 환경의 프로토콜식 대량 투여에서 예후 악화) 환자별 요인을 무시하기 때문이다.

keyChanges.topic: 최적화 단계 제한 대 자유 전략
keyChanges.detail: Reflecting large recent RCTs (e.g., CLASSIC, CLOVERS) that showed no mortality difference, ESICM 2025 makes NO recommendation for or against a systematically restrictive vs liberal fluid strategy in the optimization phase, grading this as MODERATE certainty of no effect — a more evidence-mature stance than the prior blanket lean toward fluid loading. Instead it conditionally favors an individualized, fluid-responsiveness–guided approach.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 사망률 차이를 보이지 않은 최근 대규모 RCT(예: CLASSIC, CLOVERS)를 반영해, ESICM 2025는 최적화 단계에서 체계적 제한 대 자유 전략에 대해 찬반 권고를 하지 않으며 이를 '효과 없음에 대한 중등도 확실성'으로 등급화했다 — 과거의 수액 부하 편향보다 근거가 성숙한 입장이다. 대신 수액반응성에 기반한 개별화 접근을 조건부로 선호한다.

keyChanges.detail: The guideline formalizes a RESTRICTIVE fluid strategy with permissive hypotension before hemorrhage control for trauma — conditional recommendation with MODERATE certainty for blunt trauma and LOW certainty for penetrating trauma — reflecting damage-control resuscitation evidence (lower pressure reduces re-bleeding, clot disruption, and dilutional coagulopathy). This is explicitly limited to the pre-hemorrhage-control window and excludes intraoperative/post-control care.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 외상에서 출혈 조절 전까지 permissive hypotension을 동반한 제한적 수액 전략을 공식화했다 — 둔상은 중등도 확실성, 관통상은 낮은 확실성의 조건부 권고로, damage-control resuscitation 근거(낮은 혈압이 재출혈·응고괴 붕괴·희석성 응고장애를 줄임)를 반영한다. 이는 출혈 조절 전 구간에 한정되며 수술 중·조절 후 관리는 제외된다.

keyChanges.detail: Rather than a single sepsis-centric fluid approach, the guideline issues cause-specific statements: left-sided cardiogenic shock — fluids should NOT be primary treatment; cardiac tamponade — cautious fluids only as a bridge to drainage; acute PE — fluids guided by surrogate markers of right-heart congestion; and no recommendation for ARDS-associated circulatory failure (ungraded best practice). This differentiation by shock etiology is more explicit than prior general fluid guidance.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 패혈증 중심의 단일 접근 대신 원인별 성명을 제시한다: 좌심성 심장성 쇼크는 수액을 일차 치료로 쓰지 말 것, 심장압전은 배액까지의 가교로만 신중 투여, 급성 폐색전증은 우심 울혈 대리 지표로 조절, ARDS 동반 순환부전은 권고 없음(모두 등급 미부여 모범진료). 쇼크 원인별 차등화가 과거의 포괄적 수액 지침보다 명시적이다.

augmentedSections.body_ko: 이 논평은 ESICM(‘up to 30 ml/kg’, 조건부·매우 낮은 확실성)과 Surviving Sepsis Campaign(‘at least 30 ml/kg를 3시간 내’, 약한 권고·낮은 근거)의 정면 불일치를 짚는다. SSC의 하한선 근거인 후향적 데이터의 한계로, 해당 코호트의 상당수가 엄밀한 패혈성 쇼크 기준을 충족하지 못했고(79%가 승압제 불필요, 85%가 기계환기 미시행) 대규모 RCT의 평균 용량이라는 근거도 표준편차가 ±20 ml/kg로 매우 커 개별 변동이 크다는 점을 지적한다. 결론적으로 체중 기반 고정 프로토콜보다 수액반응성 평가와 빈번한 혈역학 재평가에 기반한 개별화 소생을 옹호한다. (이는 지침 원문이 아니라 이를 논평한 2차 자료의 견해다.)
augmentedSections.sourceLabel: Initial fluid resuscitation in septic shock: Reassessing the 30 mL/kg paradigm (PMC/ScienceDirect)

card.practiceImpact: At the bedside, treat 30 ml/kg in septic shock as a ceiling and starting reference, not a mandatory bolus — titrate to the individual patient (source of sepsis, cardiac reserve, ongoing losses) and reassess frequently rather than 'chasing the number.' In the optimization phase, use dynamic fluid-responsiveness testing rather than defaulting to either liberal or restrictive protocols, since neither improves mortality. For trauma/hemorrhage, adopt permissive hypotension and minimal crystalloid until surgical/endovascular control. Explicitly de-prioritize fluids as the first move in cardiogenic shock, tamponade, and PE with RV strain — reach for the definitive intervention (inotropes/mechanical support, pericardial drainage, thrombolysis/thrombectomy) and give fluids only cautiously and guided by right-heart congestion markers.
card.practiceImpact_ko: 침상에서 패혈성 쇼크의 30 ml/kg는 의무적 볼루스가 아니라 '상한이자 출발 기준'으로 다루고, 숫자를 좇기보다 환자별(패혈증 원인, 심장 예비능, 진행 중 손실)로 적정하며 자주 재평가한다. 최적화 단계에서는 자유·제한 어느 프로토콜도 사망률을 개선하지 않으므로 동적 수액반응성 검사로 결정한다. 외상/출혈에서는 수술·중재적 지혈 전까지 permissive hypotension과 최소 결정질액을 적용한다. 심장성 쇼크, 심장압전, 우심부담이 있는 폐색전증에서는 수액을 첫 수단에서 명시적으로 후순위로 두고 확정적 치료(강심제/기계순환보조, 심낭 배액, 혈전용해/제거)를 먼저 하며 수액은 우심 울혈 지표에 따라 신중히만 준다.

published.title: Choice of resuscitation fluids in critically ill adults: key messages from the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine 2024 clinical practice guidelines.
published.abstract: The 2024 European Society of Intensive Care Medicine clinical practice guideline provide clinicians with evidence-based recommendations on intravenous fluid in critically ill adults across a range of common conditions. These guidelines aim to improve the practices of fluid therapy by adopting a global perspective that considers both clinical efficacy and resource utilization in diverse healthcare settings. The guidelines address three key questions: (1) albumin versus crystalloids, (2) balanced crystalloids versus isotonic saline, and (3) small-volume hypertonic solutions versus isotonic crystalloids. Recommendations were developed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, ensuring a rigorous and transparent evaluation of the evidence across critical outcomes. Albumin was generally not favored over crystalloids due to its lack of demonstrated mortality benefit, higher cost, and limited availability in resource-limited settings. Balanced crystalloids were suggested over isotonic saline in most scenarios due to their potential to reduce mortality and mitigate the harmful effects of hyperchloremia, although the certainty of evidence was low. Small-volume hypertonic solutions were not shown to provide significant advantages over isotonic crystalloids, leading to a preference for the latter based on very low certainty evidence. This review provides an overview of the guideline development process and a detailed summary of their recommendations, highlighting key considerations for clinical practice. The guidelines also identify critical evidence gaps in fluid therapy research, underscoring the need for future studies to refine and optimize fluid management strategies in critically ill patients.

card.title_ko: 중증 성인 환자의 소생 수액 선택 — 유럽중환자의학회(ESICM) 2024 임상진료지침 핵심 메시지
card.scope_ko: 성인 중환자(일반 중증, 패혈증, 급성호흡부전/ARDS, 외상성 뇌손상(TBI), 급성신손상(AKI), 수술 전후/출혈 위험, 간경변)에서 정맥 소생 수액의 '종류 선택'을 다루는 지침(3부작 중 Part 1). 알부민 대 결정질액, 균형결정질액 대 등장성 생리식염수, 소용량 고장액 대 등장성 결정질액의 세 가지 핵심 질문을 자원 활용까지 고려한 글로벌 관점으로 GRADE 방식으로 평가한다.
summary: Albumin vs crystalloids — general critically ill: use crystalloids rather than albumin (conditional recommendation, moderate certainty); driven by no mortality/RRT/ventilation/LOS benefit, higher cost, and limited availability.
Albumin vs crystalloids — sepsis: use crystalloids rather than albumin (conditional, moderate certainty).
Albumin vs crystalloids — acute respiratory failure and perioperative/bleeding-risk patients: use crystalloids rather than albumin (conditional, very low certainty).
Cirrhosis: use albumin rather than crystalloids (conditional, very low certainty) — the one setting where albumin is favored.
Traumatic brain injury: use isotonic saline rather than albumin (conditional, very low), and use isotonic saline rather than balanced crystalloids (conditional, very low).

Balanced crystalloids vs isotonic saline: use balanced crystalloids in general critically ill (conditional, low certainty) and in sepsis (conditional, low), and in kidney injury/AKI (conditional, very low) — to reduce mortality and mitigate hyperchloremia-related harm.

Small-volume hypertonic vs isotonic: use isotonic crystalloids rather than small-volume hypertonic solutions in general critically ill patients (conditional, very low certainty) — no demonstrated advantage for hypertonic.
summary_ko: 알부민 대 결정질액 — 일반 중증환자: 알부민보다 결정질액을 사용(조건부 권고, 중등도 확실성). 사망률·RRT·인공호흡·재원기간 이득이 없고 비용이 높으며 가용성이 제한적이기 때문.
알부민 대 결정질액 — 패혈증: 알부민보다 결정질액을 사용(조건부, 중등도 확실성).
알부민 대 결정질액 — 급성호흡부전 및 수술 전후/출혈 위험군: 알부민보다 결정질액을 사용(조건부, 매우 낮은 확실성).
간경변: 결정질액보다 알부민을 사용(조건부, 매우 낮은 확실성) — 알부민이 선호되는 유일한 상황.
외상성 뇌손상(TBI): 알부민보다 등장성 생리식염수를 사용(조건부, 매우 낮음), 그리고 균형결정질액보다 등장성 생리식염수를 사용(조건부, 매우 낮음).
균형결정질액 대 등장성 생리식염수: 일반 중증환자(조건부, 낮은 확실성)와 패혈증(조건부, 낮음), 신손상/AKI(조건부, 매우 낮음)에서 균형결정질액 사용 — 사망률 감소와 고클로라이드혈증 관련 해악 완화를 위해.
소용량 고장액 대 등장성: 일반 중증환자에서 소용량 고장액보다 등장성 결정질액을 사용(조건부, 매우 낮은 확실성) — 고장액의 이점이 입증되지 않음.

augmentedSections.heading_ko: 이 지침은 ESICM 수액치료 3부작 중 Part 1이다 (범위 맥락)
augmentedSections.body_ko: ESICM 공식 발표에 따르면 이번 '소생 수액의 선택(Part 1)'은 성인 중환자 수액치료 3부작 임상진료지침의 첫 부분이며, 나머지 두 부분은 각각 '수액의 양(amount)'과 '수액 제거(removal)'를 별도로 다룬다. 즉 지금 이 문서가 담은 세 가지 질문(알부민 대 결정질액, 균형결정질액 대 생리식염수, 고장액 대 등장액)은 수액 '종류' 축에 한정되며, 투여량·탈수액 전략은 Part 2·3에서 별도로 다뤄진다는 점을 유념해야 한다. 본 지침은 ICM(Intensive Care Medicine) 2024에 무료 접근(Online First)으로 게재되었다.

card.practiceImpact: Default to balanced crystalloids (e.g., Lactated Ringer's/Plasma-Lyte) rather than 0.9% saline for most resuscitation — general ICU, sepsis, and AKI — to avoid hyperchloremia, but keep isotonic saline as the preferred crystalloid in TBI. Stop reaching for albumin as routine resuscitation fluid in general critical illness, sepsis, ARDS, or the perioperative/bleeding-risk setting: it adds cost without a mortality benefit; reserve albumin for cirrhosis. Abandon small-volume hypertonic solutions for general resuscitation, as they show no advantage over isotonic crystalloids. Remember all recommendations are conditional with low-to-very-low certainty (moderate only for crystalloid-over-albumin in general/sepsis), so individualize and weigh cost and availability.
card.practiceImpact_ko: 대부분의 소생(일반 ICU·패혈증·AKI)에서 0.9% 생리식염수 대신 균형결정질액(Lactated Ringer's/Plasma-Lyte 등)을 기본으로 삼아 고클로라이드혈증을 피하되, TBI에서는 등장성 생리식염수를 선호 결정질액으로 유지한다. 일반 중증·패혈증·ARDS·수술전후/출혈 위험군에서 알부민을 일상적 소생 수액으로 쓰지 않는다 — 사망률 이득 없이 비용만 늘며, 알부민은 간경변에 국한한다. 소용량 고장액은 등장성 결정질액 대비 이점이 없으므로 일반 소생에서 배제한다. 모든 권고가 조건부이고 확실성이 낮음~매우 낮음(일반·패혈증에서 알부민보다 결정질액만 중등도)이므로 비용·가용성을 함께 고려해 개별화한다.

card.title_ko: 2026 AHA/ACC 성인 급성 폐색전증 평가 및 관리 가이드라인 (다학회 공동)
card.scope_ko: 18세 이상 성인의 급성 폐색전증(PE)의 진단·중증도 분류·항응고·고급치료(혈전용해/카테터/수술)·PERT 운영·퇴원 및 장기 추적까지 전 과정을 다루는, ACC/AHA가 다수 협력 학회와 함께 처음 발간한 de novo 가이드라인이다. 이전 판이 없다(2026-02-19 발표).
summary: Adopt the new AHA/ACC Acute PE Clinical Categories A–E (with subcategories) that integrate symptoms, clinical severity scores, biomarkers, RV imaging, and hemodynamics to drive prognosis and therapy, replacing the older massive/submassive/low-risk anatomic framing.

Risk-stratify with validated tools: Category B is defined by low-severity markers (e.g., PESI ≤85 / sPESI = 0 / Bova ≤4); Categories C–E denote elevated severity, incipient cardiopulmonary failure, and persistent hypotension respectively.

Diagnose using a probability-based pathway: in low-to-intermediate pretest probability obtain D-dimer (normal → PE unlikely, no imaging), and use CTPA as the standard stand-alone confirmatory imaging test.

For initial parenteral anticoagulation, use low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) in preference to unfractionated heparin (UFH); for oral therapy, use DOACs in preference to vitamin K antagonists unless contraindicated (e.g., pregnancy → LMWH/UFH).

Hospitalize Category C, D, and E patients; consider outpatient management for Category A (incidental/asymptomatic) and low-severity Category B provided immediate access to anticoagulation and structured follow-up.
Use a Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) to coordinate care and decisions about advanced interventions in higher-severity (Category C–E) PE (Class 1).

In Category E (persistent hypotension), systemic thrombolysis, catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT), mechanical thrombectomy, and surgical embolectomy are each reasonable (Class 2a) added to anticoagulation; in Category D and selected C3, these may be considered (Class 2b) with uncertain benefit.

Provide structured follow-up: contact/visit within ~1 week of discharge, reassessment by 3 months for anticoagulation duration, and screening for post-PE syndrome / CTEPH symptoms at every visit for at least 1 year, plus mental-health screening and early ambulation.
summary_ko: 새로운 AHA/ACC 급성 PE 임상 범주 A–E(하위범주 포함)를 채택한다 — 증상·임상중증도점수·바이오마커·RV 영상·혈역학을 통합해 예후와 치료를 결정하며, 기존의 massive/submassive/low-risk 해부학적 분류를 대체한다.
검증된 도구로 위험을 층화한다: Category B는 저중증도 지표(예: PESI ≤85 / sPESI = 0 / Bova ≤4)로 정의되고, Category C–E는 각각 중증도 상승, 초기 심폐부전, 지속적 저혈압을 의미한다.
확률 기반 진단 경로를 사용한다: 저–중등도 사전확률에서는 D-dimer를 측정하고(정상 → PE 가능성 낮음, 영상 불필요), 확진 영상으로 CTPA를 단독 표준검사로 사용한다.
초기 비경구 항응고는 UFH보다 LMWH를 우선하고, 경구는 금기(예: 임신 → LMWH/UFH)가 없는 한 VKA보다 DOAC를 우선한다.
Category C·D·E 환자는 입원시키고, Category A(우연·무증상)와 저중증도 Category B는 즉각적 항응고 접근성과 구조화된 추적이 확보되면 외래 관리를 고려한다.
중등도 이상(Category C–E) PE에서 치료 조율과 고급중재 결정을 위해 PERT(폐색전 대응팀)를 운영한다(Class 1).
Category E(지속적 저혈압)에서는 항응고에 더해 전신혈전용해·카테터혈전용해(CDT)·기계적 혈전제거·수술적 색전제거술이 각각 합리적이며(Class 2a), Category D 및 선택된 C3에서는 고려할 수 있으나(Class 2b) 이득은 불확실하다.
구조화된 추적을 제공한다: 퇴원 후 약 1주 내 접촉/방문, 3개월까지 항응고 지속기간 재평가, 최소 1년간 매 방문마다 post-PE 증후군/CTEPH 증상 선별, 그리고 정신건강 선별과 조기 보행.

keyChanges.detail: Previous paradigm: dichotomous/anatomic 'massive vs submassive vs low-risk' stratification centered on hemodynamics and clot burden → New: an integrative 5-level AHA/ACC Acute PE Clinical Category system (A–E, with subcategories) built on clinical severity scores, biomarkers, RV imaging, and hemodynamics, shifting focus from anatomic clot burden to physiopathologic impact. Reason: to sharpen prognosis and match therapy to physiology, and to separate incidental/asymptomatic PE from truly high-risk presentations that older schemes lumped together.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 이전: 혈역학·혈전량 중심의 이분법적/해부학적 'massive vs submassive vs low-risk' 분류 → 신규: 임상중증도점수·바이오마커·RV 영상·혈역학을 통합한 5단계 AHA/ACC 급성 PE 임상 범주(A–E, 하위범주 포함)로, 초점을 해부학적 혈전량에서 병태생리학적 영향으로 이동. 이유: 예후를 정밀화하고 치료를 생리와 맞추며, 기존 체계가 뭉뚱그렸던 우연·무증상 PE를 진짜 고위험 표현형과 분리하기 위함.

keyChanges.detail: Previous 'low-risk' bucket → New Category A (incidental/asymptomatic PE) is distinguished from Category B (symptomatic, low severity: e.g., PESI ≤85 / sPESI = 0 / Bova ≤4). Both A and B are considered candidates for outpatient/early-discharge management provided immediate access to anticoagulation and structured follow-up. Reason: explicit thresholds and follow-up safeguards let more low-severity patients avoid hospitalization safely.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 이전의 'low-risk' 묶음 → 신규로 Category A(우연·무증상 PE)를 Category B(증상 있음, 저중증도: 예 PESI ≤85 / sPESI = 0 / Bova ≤4)와 구분. A와 B 모두 즉각적 항응고 접근성과 구조화된 추적이 있으면 외래/조기퇴원 관리 후보로 간주. 이유: 명시적 기준과 추적 안전장치로 더 많은 저중증도 환자가 안전하게 입원을 피할 수 있게 함.

keyChanges.detail: Previous practice prioritized systemic thrombolysis as the default reperfusion therapy for high-risk PE → New: in Category E, systemic thrombolysis, catheter-directed thrombolysis, mechanical thrombectomy, and surgical embolectomy are each placed as reasonable (Class 2a) added to anticoagulation, without a fixed hierarchy; in Category D and selected C3 they are Class 2b ('may be considered', uncertain benefit). Described as the first North American guideline to equate these modalities rather than default to systemic lysis. Reason: growing catheter-based options and PERT-driven, patient-specific selection.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 이전에는 고위험 PE의 기본 재관류로 전신혈전용해를 우선 → 신규: Category E에서 전신혈전용해·CDT·기계적 혈전제거·수술적 색전제거술을 고정된 위계 없이 각각 합리적(Class 2a, 항응고에 추가)으로 배치; Category D 및 선택된 C3에서는 Class 2b('고려 가능', 이득 불확실). 전신용해를 기본으로 두지 않고 이들 방식을 동등하게 놓은 첫 북미 가이드라인으로 기술됨. 이유: 카테터 기반 옵션의 확대와 PERT 주도의 환자 맞춤 선택.

keyChanges.detail: Previous: PERT was an informal, institution-dependent practice → New: multidisciplinary PERT is formally embedded as a Class 1 recommendation to coordinate care and decisions about acute interventions in higher-severity (Category C–E) PE. Reason: to improve timeliness and consistency of advanced-therapy decisions.
keyChanges.detail_ko: 이전: PERT는 비공식적이고 기관 재량에 맡겨진 관행 → 신규: 다학제 PERT를 Class 1 권고로 공식 편입하여 중등도 이상(Category C–E) PE의 치료 조율과 급성 중재 결정을 담당. 이유: 고급치료 결정의 신속성과 일관성 향상.

keyChanges.detail: Previous guidance was limited on structured post-PE follow-up → New: standardized pathway with contact/visit within ~1 week, reassessment of anticoagulation duration by 3 months, and screening for CTEPH / post-PE syndrome symptoms at every visit for at least 1 year, plus mental-health screening (depression/anxiety/PTSD), early ambulation, travel precautions, and contraception counseling. Reason: patient-centered outcomes established as the standard for follow-up care.

card.practiceImpact: At the bedside, EM/CCM clinicians should stop reflexively labeling PE as 'submassive/massive' and instead assign an A–E clinical category using PESI/sPESI/Bova, troponin/BNP, RV imaging, and hemodynamics — this single classification now drives disposition (discharge A–B vs admit C–E) and therapy intensity. Activate a PERT early for Category C–E, and recognize that in Category E systemic lysis no longer automatically outranks catheter-directed or mechanical options — choice is individualized (Class 2a), while Category D/C3 interventions remain Class 2b with uncertain benefit. Default to LMWH over UFH and DOACs over VKAs, use D-dimer/CTPA probability pathways to limit unnecessary imaging, and build in structured follow-up (1-week contact, 3-month anticoagulation review, ≥1-year CTEPH and mental-health screening) before discharge.
card.practiceImpact_ko: 병상에서 EM/CCM 임상의는 PE를 반사적으로 'submassive/massive'로 부르는 습관을 버리고, PESI/sPESI/Bova·트로포닌/BNP·RV 영상·혈역학으로 A–E 임상 범주를 부여해야 한다 — 이 하나의 분류가 이제 처치 방향(A–B 퇴원 vs C–E 입원)과 치료 강도를 결정한다. Category C–E에서는 PERT를 조기 가동하고, Category E에서는 전신용해가 카테터·기계적 옵션을 자동으로 앞서지 않음(개별화, Class 2a)을, Category D/C3 중재는 여전히 Class 2b로 이득이 불확실함을 인식해야 한다. UFH보다 LMWH, VKA보다 DOAC를 기본으로 하고, D-dimer/CTPA 확률 경로로 불필요한 영상을 줄이며, 퇴원 전 구조화된 추적(1주 접촉·3개월 항응고 재검토·1년 이상 CTEPH 및 정신건강 선별)을 반드시 마련한다.

rejected.title: [Best practice deployment of lead emergency physicians in Germany - A Delphi study: A structured consensus process among EMS medical directors].
rejected.journal: Zeitschrift fur Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualitat im Gesundheitswesen
rejected.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Complex emergency operations in prehospital care, such as mass casualty incidents (MCI), place special demands on the deployment of the Leading Emergency Physician (LNA). Uniform national standards for LNA appointment are currently lacking. This study aimed to develop a consensus-based best practice model and to highlight the relevance of the new curriculum of the German Medical Association (BÄK) for LNA qualification.
METHODS: In two Delphi rounds, 20 theses were evaluated to determine consensus (K = agreement), neutrality (0 = abstention), or dissent (D = disagreement). The topics included professional qualification as well as structural, material, and organizational resources. Participants were N = 56 medical directors of emergency medical services (ÄLRD) attending the BV-ÄLRD annual meeting in 2024.
RESULTS: Broad consensus was reached that LNA should hold a specialist qualification (K = 96%) and complete specific continuing education (K = 96%). Regular activity as an emergency physician (K = 93%) and participation in exercises (K = 93%) were considered essential. Structural requirements such as fixed duty rosters (K = 89%) and defined alerting criteria (K = 96%) achieved high levels of agreement. Standard leadership tools (K = 96%) and personal protective equipment (K = 100%) were also rated as essential. An advisory function outside MCI scenarios was a controversial debate topic (K = 44%, 0 = 22%, D = 34%).
DISCUSSION: The results provide consensus-based recommendations for a quality-assured LNA appointment with standardized qualification and organizational structures. Standardized measures improve service readiness and quality of LNA deployment and emphasize the importance of a national curriculum and structural requirements.

rejected.title: Treatment of rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease: An appraisal of the 2023 ACR/CHEST guideline.
rejected.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize the current treatment landscape of rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) in the context of the recent 2023 American College of Rheumatology/American College of Chest Physicians guideline for ILD treatment in systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
RECENT FINDINGS: The guideline conditionally recommends mycophenolate, azathioprine, and rituximab for first-line RA-ILD therapy, with cyclophosphamide and short-term glucocorticoids as additional options. For RA-ILD progression after first line, mycophenolate, rituximab, nintedanib, tocilizumab, cyclophosphamide, and pirfenidone are conditionally recommended, while long-term glucocorticoids are conditionally recommended against. Only three randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolled patients with RA-ILD (total n=217). All other recommendations for RA-ILD were based on RCTs for other diseases or observational data. Antifibrotics might be particularly effective for patients with RA-ILD and the usual interstitial pneumonia pattern (RA-UIP). There is uncertainty of the utility of azathioprine and glucocorticoids in RA-UIP since these medications had worse outcomes compared to placebo in an RCT of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. RA-ILD treatment decisions should consider articular activity, ILD activity, comorbidities, and potential for infection.
SUMMARY: We summarized the current treatment landscape for RA-ILD. Since only three RCTs included patients with RA-ILD, most guideline recommendations were conditional and based on low-quality evidence. This highlights the urgent need for additional high-quality RCT data for efficacy and safety of anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic medications for RA-ILD.

rejected.title: Use of COVID-19 Vaccines for Persons Aged ≥6 Months: Recommendations of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices - United States, 2024-2025.
rejected.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
rejected.abstract: COVID-19 vaccination provides additional protection against severe COVID-19-associated illness and death. Since September 2023, 2023-2024 Formula monovalent XBB.1-strain COVID-19 vaccines have been recommended for use in the United States for all persons aged ≥6 months. However, SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, and since winter 2023-2024, Omicron JN.1 lineage strains of SARS-CoV-2, including the JN.1 strain and the KP.2 strain, have been widely circulating in the United States. Further, COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness is known to wane. On June 27, 2024, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccination with a Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved or authorized vaccine for all persons aged ≥6 months. On August 22, 2024, FDA approved the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccines by Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech (based on the KP.2 strain) for use in persons aged ≥12 years and authorized these vaccines for use in children aged 6 months-11 years under Emergency Use Authorization (EUA). On August 30, 2024, FDA authorized 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine by Novavax (based on the JN.1 strain) for use in persons aged ≥12 years under EUA. ACIP will continue to evaluate new evidence as it becomes available and will update recommendations as needed.

rejected.title: Informing pandemic management in Germany with trustworthy living evidence syntheses and guideline development: lessons learned from the COVID-19 evidence ecosystem.
rejected.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We present the 'COVID-19 evidence ecosystem' (CEOsys) as a German network to inform pandemic management and to support clinical and public health decision-making. We discuss challenges faced when organizing the ecosystem and derive lessons learned for similar networks acting during pandemics or health-related crises.
STUDY DESIGN AND SETTING: Bringing together 18 university hospitals and additional institutions, CEOsys key activities included research prioritization, conducting living systematic reviews (LSRs), supporting evidence-based (living) guidelines, knowledge translation (KT), detecting research gaps, and deriving recommendations, backed by technical infrastructure and capacity building.
RESULTS: CEOsys rapidly produced 31 high-quality evidence syntheses and supported three living guidelines on COVID-19-related topics, while also developing methodological procedures. Challenges included CEOsys' late initiation in relation to the pandemic outbreak, the delayed prioritization of research questions, the continuously evolving COVID-19-related evidence, and establishing a technical infrastructure. Methodological-clinical tandems, the cooperation with national guideline groups and international collaborations were key for efficiency.
CONCLUSION: CEOsys provided a proof-of-concept for a functioning evidence ecosystem at the national level. Lessons learned include that similar networks should, among others, involve methodological and clinical key stakeholders early on, aim for (inter)national collaborations, and systematically evaluate their value. We particularly call for a sustainable network.

rejected.title: The Association Between Meeting Physical Activity Guidelines and Mental Health Among High-School Students in the United States During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
rejected.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
rejected.abstract:
PURPOSE: Physical activity (PA) is associated with mental health outcomes in high-school students, yet many students do not meet the recommended PA levels. Furthermore, both PA levels and mental health were severely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The aim of this study was to assess whether the number of PA recommendations students met during the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with their self-reported mental health (including their experiences with stress, anxiety, and depression) during the COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: Students completed the Adolescent Behaviors and Experiences Survey, where they reported PA behaviors, mental health, and COVID-19-related experiences (as control variables) during the pandemic.
RESULTS: Each PA recommendation that was met was associated with a 17% decrease in the odds of students self-reporting that they experienced stress, anxiety, or depression most of the time or always during the COVID-19 pandemic.
DISCUSSION: Students should be provided with opportunities to participate in PA to obtain the physical and mental health benefits, especially in the event of a crisis like the pandemic.

rejected.title: ChatGPT as a Clinical Decision Maker for Urolithiasis: Compliance with the Current European Association of Urology Guidelines.
rejected.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Generative artificial intelligence models are among the most promising and widely used tools used in health care. This review investigates GPT-4 answers to decision-making questions regarding the diagnosis and treatment of urolithiasis across several clinical settings and their correspondence to the current European Association of Urology (EAU) guidelines.
METHODS: In March 2024, the GPT-4 model was asked 11 questions, containing a brief description of a patient with urolithiasis. All questions were grouped according to urolithiasis care step: diagnosis, urgent care, scheduled intervention, and metaphylaxis. When responses were received, compliance with the current EAU guidelines was assessed by experienced urologists.
KEY FINDINGS AND LIMITATIONS: Although all responses were provided with information that corresponded to EAU guidelines, six of the 11 answers were associated with missed guideline-provided parts, and incorrect data were given in eight of the 11 answers. GPT-4 is relatively safe in the initial diagnostic flow of patients suspected of having stones within the urinary tract and during treatment planning; however, its understanding of all the nuances of metaphylaxis leaves much to be desired and is far from the dogma given in the EAU guidelines. Moreover, GPT-4 knowledge of strategy and algorithm is not always aligned with the EAU guidelines.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Despite the fact that from the perspective of patients with urolithiasis, GPT-4 is capable of answering their questions well, the specificity of questions from urologists is labor intensive for its current version, and necessitates the ability to interpret it correctly and further attempts to improve it. While some aspects of diagnostics are more accurate, these struggle with surgical planning and algorithms in line with the EAU guidelines.
PATIENT SUMMARY: The generative artificial intelligence (AI) model GPT-4 is capable of answering urology-related questions, but lacks detailed responses. Although some aspects of the diagnostics are accurate, knowledge of surgical planning is not in line with the European Association of Urology guidelines. Future improvements should focus on efforts to enhance the accuracy, reliability, and clinical relevance of AI tools in urology.

rejected.title: ESPEN practical guideline on clinical nutrition in hospitalized patients with acute or chronic kidney disease.
rejected.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hospitalized patients often have acute kidney disease (AKD) or chronic kidney disease (CKD), with important metabolic and nutritional consequences. Moreover, in case kidney replacement therapy (KRT) is started, the possible impact on nutritional requirements cannot be neglected. On this regard, the present guideline aims to provide evidence-based recommendations for clinical nutrition in hospitalized patients with KD.
METHODS: The standard operating procedure for ESPEN guidelines was used. Clinical questions were defined in both the PICO format, and organized in subtopics when needed, and in non-PICO questions for the more general topics. The literature search was from January 1st, 1999 until January 1st, 2020. Each question led to one or more recommendation/statement and related commentaries. Existing evidence was graded, as well as recommendations and statements were developed and agreed upon in a multistage consensus process.
RESULTS: The present guideline provides 32 evidence-based recommendations and 8 statements, defining how to assess nutritional status, how to define patients at risk, how to choose the route of feeding, and how to integrate nutrition with KRT. In the final online voting, a strong consensus was reached in 84% at least of recommendations and 100% of statements.
CONCLUSION: The presence of KD in hospitalized patients identifies a highly heterogeneous group of subjects with widely varying nutrient needs and intakes. Considering the high nutritional risk related with this clinical condition, an individualized approach consisting of nutritional status evaluation and monitoring, frequent evaluation of nutritional requirements, and careful integration with KRT should be planned to avoid both underfeeding and overfeeding. Practical recommendations and statements were developed, aiming at defining suggestions for everyday clinical practice in the individualization of nutritional support in this patient setting. Literature areas with scarce or without evidence were also identified, thus requiring further basic or clinical research.

rejected.title: Avoiding the use of long-term parenteral support in patients without intestinal failure: A position paper from the European Society of Clinical Nutrition & Metabolism, the European Society of Neurogastroenterology and Motility and the Rome Foundation for Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction.
rejected.abstract: The role of long-term parenteral support in patients with underlying benign conditions who do not have intestinal failure (IF) is contentious, not least since there are clear benefits in utilising the oral or enteral route for nutritional support. Furthermore, the risks of long-term home parenteral nutrition (HPN) are significant, with significant impacts on morbidity and mortality. There has, however, been a recent upsurge of the use of HPN in patients with conditions such as gastro-intestinal neuromuscular disorders, opioid bowel dysfunction, disorders of gut-brain interaction and possibly eating disorders, who do not have IF. As a result, the European Society of Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN), the European Society of Neuro-gastroenterology and Motility (ESNM) and the Rome Foundation for Disorders of Gut Brain Interaction felt that a position statement is required to clarify - and hopefully reduce the potential for harm associated with - the use of long-term parenteral support in patients without IF. Consensus opinion is that HPN should not be prescribed for patients without IF, where the oral and/or enteral route can be utilised. On the rare occasions that PN commencement is required to treat life-threatening malnutrition in conditions such as those listed above, it should only be prescribed for a time-limited period to achieve nutritional safety, while the wider multi-disciplinary team focus on more appropriate biopsychosocial holistic and rehabilitative approaches to manage the patient's primary underlying condition.

rejected.title: Assessment of ChatGPT's Compliance with ESC-Acute Coronary Syndrome Management Guidelines at 30-Day Intervals.
rejected.abstract: Despite ongoing advancements in healthcare, acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. The 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines have introduced significant improvements in ACS management. Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI), particularly models like ChatGPT, is showing promise in supporting clinical decision-making and education.  This study evaluates the performance of ChatGPT-v4 in adhering to ESC guidelines for ACS management over a 30-day interval. Based on ESC guidelines, a dataset of 100 questions was used to assess ChatGPT's accuracy and consistency. The questions were divided into binary (true/false) and multiple-choice formats. The AI's responses were initially evaluated and then re-evaluated after 30 days, using accuracy and consistency as primary metrics.  ChatGPT's accuracy in answering ACS-related binary and multiple-choice questions was evaluated at baseline and after 30 days. For binary questions, accuracy was 84% initially and 86% after 30 days, with no significant change ( = 0.564). Cohen's Kappa was 0.94, indicating excellent agreement. Multiple-choice question accuracy was 80% initially, improving to 84% after 30 days, also without significant change ( = 0.527). Cohen's Kappa was 0.93, reflecting similarly high consistency. These results suggest stable AI performance with minor fluctuations.  Despite variations in performance on binary and multiple-choice questions, ChatGPT shows significant promise as a clinical support tool in ACS management. However, it is crucial to consider limitations such as fluctuations and hallucinations, which could lead to severe issues in clinical applications.

rejected.title: Long-term monitoring and treatment of venous thromboembolic disease: recommendations of the Thromboembolic Disease Group of the Spanish Society of Internal Medicine 2024.
rejected.abstract: Venous thromboembolim (VTE) is a highly prevalent condition that requires long-term monitoring and treatment. This monitoring includes: 1) completing the etiological study and determining the risk of VTE recurrence; 2) establishing the optimal duration of anticoagulant treatment, as well as the type of therapy and its dosage; 3) estimating the risk of bleeding, and 4) identifying the occurrence of chronic complications. This consensus document, prepared by the VTE Group of the Spanish Society of Internal Medicine (SEMI), aims to update and establish consensus recommendations on these aspects. The document focuses on four aspects of management: the first includes risk factors for VTE recurrence after an unprovoked VTE episode and describes the predictive scores of VTE recurrence; the second focuses on risk factors for bleeding; the third provides recommendations for long-term follow-up in VTE, addressing specific considerations for screening chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and post-thrombotic syndrome of the lower limbs; and the fourth provides guidance on the optimal duration of extended anticoagulant treatment, as well as the type of therapy and its dosage. For each area, an exhaustive literature review was conducted, analyzing the updated VTE clinical guidelines and recent studies. This document is intended to be a guide in the long-term management of VTE based on the most current knowledge.

rejected.title: The 2024 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation: A Viewpoint from a Practicing Clinician's Perspective.
rejected.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a complex disease requiring a multidomain and (usually) long-term management, thus posing a significant burden to patients with AF, practitioners, and health care system. Unlike cardiovascular conditions with a narrow referral pathway (e.g., acute coronary syndrome), AF may be first detected by a wide range of specialties (often noncardiology) or a general practitioner. Since timely initiated optimal management is essential for the prevention of AF-related complications, a concise and simple guidance is essential for practitioners managing AF patients, regardless of their specialty. Guideline-adherent management of patients with AF has been shown to translate to improved patient outcomes compared with guideline-nonadherent treatment. To facilitate guideline implementation in routine clinical practice, a good guideline document on AF should introduce only evidence-based new recommendations, while avoiding arbitrary changes, which may be confusing to practitioners. Herein, we discuss the main changes in the 2024 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) AF Guidelines relative to the previous 2020 ESC document. Whether the updates and new recommendations issued by the new guidelines will translate in high adherence in clinical practice (and hence improved prognosis of patients with AF) will need to be addressed in upcoming years.

Is the NICE Guideline for maintenance fluid therapy in adults in hospital appropriate?
rejected.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence's (NICE) Guideline for Maintenance Fluid Therapy in Adults in Hospital is widely used, but the recommendations have not been evaluated properly. In this study, we investigated whether the recommendation of providing 25-30 mL/kg/day of fluid and 1 mmol/kg each of sodium and potassium is sufficient for human needs.
METHODS: First, we calculated the distribution of fluid between the extracellular fluid volume (ECV) and intracellular fluid volume (ICV) during a cross-over infusion experiment where 12 volunteers received 25 mL/kg/day of either a high-sodium (154 mmol/L) or low-sodium (54 mmol/L) solution over 48 h. Second, urine samples from 719 volunteers and clinical patients were used to quantify their renal water conservation and excretion of sodium and potassium. Third, retrospective analysis of a diet study was used to extrapolate how large the fluid intake and the electrolyte excretion likely had been in the 719 volunteers and hospital patients who delivered urine.
RESULTS: The high-sodium fluid maintained the ECV but the ICV had decreased by 1.3 L after 48 h. The low-sodium fluid resulted in a volume deficit of 1.7 L that equally affected the ECV and the ICV. Regression equations based on the diet study suggested that the daily intake of water in the 719 subjects averaged 2.6 L and that 2 mmol/kg of sodium and 1 mmol/kg of potassium was excreted.
CONCLUSION: The NICE guideline recommends too little water and sodium for a human to adequately maintain the ECV and ICV.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATIONS: EudraCT 2016-001846-24 and ISRCTN 12215472.
